items.title: Karl Berger interviewed by Monk Rowe, Woodstock, New York, August 11, 2014
items.q: Ahmad Jamal was a great musician like that. He would do that all the time.

ctx.x: So this is why the art of not playing is sort of what interests me the most. What do I need — what is not needed. So there is always the process of writing and then as little as necessary to make the music happening, and still then taking out some notes. Until you hear a structure that you know is going to work by itself. Like to me it satisfies me. But it has enough room for people to have all kind of fantasies around it of what it could be. People fill in. People love to come and fill in with their minds. So…
I couldn’t agree more. I work with a drummer now who does something that no other drummer —
